title: Turning down the safe job
situation: You have a stable bank job offer, and your parents have already told relatives. You want to turn it down for a lower-paying startup role in Bengaluru. It's after dinner, and your father has just asked about the joining date.
goal: Tell him your decision, and leave him worried but not hurt.

partner.name: Papa
partner.hiddenWant: Reassurance. His nephew Pinku's startup failed badly, and he watched that family struggle. He's proud of you but rarely says it.
digsInWhen: You sound like you haven't planned

rubric.name: Showed respect
rubric.tip: Start with what his support made possible, before the news.

rubric.name: Showed a real plan
rubric.tip: Have three numbers ready: savings, pay difference, and a date to reassess.

rubric.name: Listened to the worry
rubric.tip: Ask "What worries you most?" and let him answer fully.

rubric.name: Stayed clear on the decision
rubric.description: Said it as a decision, warmly
rubric.tip: State it as a decision, not a question, while staying warm.

partnerLine.guarded: Offer letter came? When's the joining date?
partnerLine.neutral: So the offer letter came? Good, good. When's the joining date? Your mother wants to call your Mausi.
partnerLine.open: So the offer letter came! Very good. When's the joining date? Your mother wants to call your Mausi.

choices.text: It came, Papa. Before we tell anyone, can I talk to you about it? I've been thinking a lot, and I want your view.
choices.reaction: Talk about what? It's a good offer.
choices.coachNote: Asking for his view before the news makes him a partner, not an opponent.

choices.text: Actually, Papa, don't tell Mausi yet. I might not take it.
choices.reaction: Might not take it? What does that mean?
choices.coachNote: Honest, but it lands as a surprise and starts with a "don't."
choices.betterLine: It came, Papa. Before we tell anyone, can I talk to you about it?

choices.text: Papa, I'm not joining the bank. I've already accepted the startup offer.
choices.coachNote: Opening with a done deal skips him entirely. The decision may be right, but the order hurts.
choices.betterLine: It came, Papa. Before we tell anyone, I want your view on something.

partnerLine.guarded: What is there to discuss? A bank job is a bank job. Security for life.
partnerLine.neutral: What is there to think about? It's a bank. Stable. Sharma uncle's son joined SBI, and look at him now.
partnerLine.open: Okay, tell me. But a bank job is a good thing, beta. Sharma uncle's son joined SBI. Look at him now.

choices.text: It is a good offer, and I know I have it because of everything you and Mummy did. But I got another offer, from a startup in Bengaluru, and I want to take it.
choices.coachNote: You gave credit first and stated the decision plainly, so it sounds considered, not rebellious.

choices.text: I know, but I don't want to be Sharma uncle's son. I want something more exciting.
choices.coachNote: Wanting more is fair, but "exciting" sounds like a whim to someone who values security.
choices.betterLine: It's a good offer, and I have it because of you. But I want to take a startup role in Bengaluru.

trigger.label: You sound like you haven't planned

choices.text: Papa, that's such an old way of thinking. Nobody cares about bank jobs anymore.
choices.reaction: Old way of thinking. Okay. This old way of thinking paid for your college.
choices.coachNote: It dismisses his whole life's logic, so now he's defending himself instead of listening.
choices.betterLine: It is a good offer, and I have it because of you. But I want to take a different one.

partnerLine.guarded: And when it shuts down in a year? Then what? You'll come back home?
partnerLine.neutral: These startups shut down overnight, beta. And the pay is less, na?
partnerLine.open: I'm just worried, beta. These startups close overnight. And the pay is less?

choices.text: It's about 20% less. I've saved enough for six months, they're funded for two years, and if it's not working in a year, I'll apply to banks again.
choices.coachNote: Numbers and a fallback turn his fear into something he can check, which is what he needed.

choices.text: It'll be fine, Papa. Don't worry so much.
choices.reaction: Telling me not to worry doesn't make me worry less.
choices.coachNote: Reassurance without details sounds like you haven't thought about the risk.
choices.betterLine: It's about 20% less. I've saved six months, and I'll reassess in a year.

trigger.label: You sound like you haven't planned

choices.text: You just don't understand how the industry works now.
choices.reaction: Then explain it. Don't just tell me I don't understand.
choices.coachNote: It shuts him out right when he's asking a real question.
choices.betterLine: It's about 20% less. Here's my plan: six months saved, and I'll reassess in a year.

partnerLine.guarded: Do what you want. You've decided anyway.
partnerLine.neutral: Hmm. I still don't like it. What will I tell people?
partnerLine.open: Hmm. I still don't fully like it. But okay. What do we tell your Mausi?

choices.text: I know this is hard. What worries you most about it? I'd rather hear it from you than guess.
choices.reaction: ...Pinku. I saw what happened to Pinku's family. I don't want that for you.
choices.coachNote: One open question reached the real fear, which no amount of numbers would have.

choices.text: Just tell them I'm working at a tech company in Bengaluru. That's it.
choices.coachNote: Practical, but it answers the surface question and skips the worry underneath.
choices.betterLine: I know this is hard. What worries you most about it?

choices.text: Honestly, Papa, why do you care so much what relatives think?
choices.reaction: Because they're our family. Forget it. Do what you want.
choices.coachNote: Questioning his values at the end reopens the fight you'd almost settled.
choices.betterLine: I know this is hard. What worries you most?

endings.guarded: Do what you want. I'm going to sleep.
endings.neutral: Okay. Send me the offer letter. I want to read it myself.
endings.open: Okay. I'll tell your mother. And beta... send me the company's name. I want to read about it.
